limit_order_added_occurred.meaning: a limit order was added to the book via addOrderToBook (which calls _updateBookPostOrder then _updateLimitPostOrder)

order_stored_before_limit_update_occurre.meaning: the order was already added to storage in _updateBookPostOrder before _updateLimitPostOrder was called

order_passed_as_memory_occurred.meaning: the order passed into _updateLimitPostOrder is of type memory

prev_order_id_persisted_in_storage.meaning: the added order's prevOrderId is persisted in the stored order (storage) rather than only in a memory copy
prev_order_id_persisted_in_storage.checkpoint: after _updateLimitPostOrder completes for the added order

prev_order_id_not_saved_observed.meaning: the added order's prevOrderId is not saved with it in storage (stored order keeps its original value)
prev_order_id_not_saved_observed.checkpoint: after _updateLimitPostOrder completes for the added order

assumptions: The order added to the book is the same order whose prevOrderId is at issue; the report does not distinguish multiple concurrent orders.
The stored order's prevOrderId is the observable field of interest; the report does not give its numeric value, only that it should be persisted.
No authorization or caller restriction on addOrderToBook is stated, so none is encoded.

unresolved.description: Report does not state the concrete prevOrderId value or the expected linked-list neighbor ids, so the correspondence is encoded as a grounded Boolean over the persistence relation rather than an integer equality.

limitations: Only the prevOrderId-not-saved impact is formalized; downstream order-loss and removal-head effects are handled in separate passes.
The persistence relation is represented by a grounded Boolean because the report gives no numeric prevOrderId values to compare.
The removal scenario (order_removed_from_limit) is not part of this claim's P because it is a later conditional event, not a before-condition of the add.
